title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: cloud storage, cloud service and Microsoft Fabric indicators as Data leaks policy triggers
summary: Hold: the policy-creation route omits choices in the wizard, and the stated administrator requirement excludes other roles Microsoft permits. The statement that scoring cannot start before a trigger also omits Microsoft's manual-enrolment exception. The roadmap dates, indicator descriptions and processing-unit billing are supported.

claims.claim: Cloud storage, cloud service and Microsoft Fabric indicators are supported as Data leaks policy triggers.
claims.quote: With this update, the indicators belonging to cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (Azure, Amazon Web Services) and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI, Lakehouse) will be supported as triggers in Data leaks policy.

claims.claim: Learn documents cloud storage, cloud service and Fabric indicators as built-in indicators.
claims.quote:
### Built-in indicators
Insider Risk Management includes the following built-in indicators.
#### Cloud storage indicators

claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators detect discovery, collection, exfiltration and deletion in Google Drive, Box and Dropbox.
claims.quote:
Use cloud storage indicators to detect the following activities in Google Drive, Box, and Dropbox:
1. Discovery
2. Collection
3. Exfiltration
4. Deletion (impact)

claims.where: What's changing: cloud service activities; Scope: Services
claims.claim: Cloud service indicators cover Amazon S3 and Azure SQL Server and Storage.
claims.quote: These indicators include policy indicators for Amazon S3 and Azure (SQL Server and Storage) that you can use to detect techniques used to avoid detection or risky activities.

claims.claim: Cloud service indicators include disabling trace logs.
claims.quote:
These techniques might include:
- Disabling trace logs

claims.claim: Cloud service indicators include changes to SQL Server firewall rules.
claims.quote: Updating or deleting SQL Server firewall rules

claims.where: What's changing: Fabric activities; Scope: Services
claims.claim: Fabric indicators cover Power BI and Lakehouse workloads.
claims.quote: These indicators include policy indicators for Microsoft Fabric workloads such as Power BI and Lakehouse.

claims.claim: Fabric indicators include viewing Power BI reports.
claims.quote: Figure out the environment (for example, viewing Power BI reports and dashboards).

claims.claim: Fabric indicators include downloading Power BI reports.
claims.quote: Gather data of interest (for example, downloading Power BI reports).

claims.claim: Fabric indicators include downgrading or removing sensitivity labels on Power BI or Lakehouse assets.
claims.quote: Obfuscate the data gathered or change protection (for example, downgrading or removing sensitivity labels of Power BI or Lakehouse assets).

claims.claim: Fabric indicators include sharing Lakehouse data outside the organisation.
claims.quote: Exfiltrate the data (for example, sharing Lakehouse data with people outside the organization).

claims.claim: Data leaks and Data leaks by priority users offer an exfiltration activity triggering event with one or more selected indicators.
claims.quote: If you select the User performs an exfiltration activity triggering event option, you must select one or more of the listed indicators for the policy triggering event.

claims.claim: Indicators disabled for the organisation cannot be selected until enabled.
claims.quote: If you're unable to select a listed indicator or sequence, it's because they aren't currently enabled for your organization. To make them available to select and assign to the policy, select the Turn on indicators prompt.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly name cloud storage, cloud service and Fabric indicators in its list of exfiltration trigger options.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Fabric Insider Risk Management indicators prerequisites audit settings triggers cloud storage trigger list. Read configure and policy-indicators pages, including all passages mentioning triggers, Fabric and cloud indicators; no explicit list naming these trigger options.

claims.where: What's changing: final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The Get started page still labels cloud indicators as preview.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management includes the following cloud indicators (preview):

claims.claim: Until a trigger fires, a Data leaks policy does not score a user.
claims.quote: If you add a user to an Insider Risk Management policy but the user doesn't have a triggering event, the policy doesn't evaluate the user's activity unless you manually add the user in the Users dashboard.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'A policy does not evaluate a user without a triggering event unless an administrator manually adds the user in the Users dashboard.' This exception is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-policy-templates#policy-template-prerequisites-and-triggering-events.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: IRM is included in Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, the named Purview suites, Defender + Purview Suite FLW and the E5/A5/F5/G5 IRM add-on.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, and Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Insider Risk Management

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: product licensing with complementary pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.where: front matter: cost; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: These indicators are metered on data security processing units, making cost variable.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management indicators that detect activity in cloud storage apps (Box, Dropbox, Google Drive), cloud services (AWS, Azure), and Microsoft Fabric (Power BI) are billed on data security processing units.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: One IRM processing unit represents the compute to process 10,000 user activities.
claims.quote: For Insider Risk Management, a processing unit represents the compute required to process 10,000 such user activities. Billing is based on the number of processing units utilized.

claims.claim: The data security processing-unit meter is measured daily.
claims.quote: | Insider Risk Management | Detect risky behavior for non-Microsoft 365 locations when using Cloud and generative AI policy indicators | Data Security processing unit as measured on a daily basis |

claims.where: Governance controls; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: turn off indicators
claims.claim: Global policy-indicator settings govern indicator availability across all insider risk policies.
claims.quote: Global settings indicators: Indicators enabled in global settings for Insider Risk Management define both the indicators available for configuration in policies and the types of events signals collected by Insider Risk Management.

claims.claim: Only Data leaks and Data leaks by priority users have customisable triggering events.
claims.quote: You can only modify triggering events for policies created from the Data leaks or Data leaks by priority users templates. Policies created from all other templates don't have customizable triggering indicators or events.
claims.fix: Replace the broad 'only' statements with: 'The Data leaks and Data leaks by priority users templates offer the User performs an exfiltration activity triggering event option.' The cited Get started page also documents Communication Compliance and HR event choices for Data leaks by risky users and Security policy violations by risky users at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure#step-6-required-create-an-insider-risk-management-policy.

claims.claim: Policy indicators are reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Insider Risk Management > Settings > Policy indicators.

claims.claim: The printed creation route goes directly from Policy template > Data leaks to Triggers for this policy.
claims.quote: On the Policy template page, choose a policy category and then select the template for the new policy. I don't want to specify priority content right now. Select this option to skip the priority content detail pages in the workflow.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path with 'Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy > Policy template > policy category > Data leaks > Content to prioritize > I don't want to specify priority content right now > Triggers for this policy > User performs an exfiltration activity triggering event'. Add to the note: 'This route skips optional priority content; complete the name fields and choose the policy user scope on the intervening wizard pages.' The category choice and priority-content branch are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure#step-6-required-create-an-insider-risk-management-policy.

claims.claim: Settings > Account details in the Microsoft Purview portal is the entry to subscription-based pay-as-you-go enablement.
claims.quote: Select Get Started in the ribbon menu to start the process. This can also be done from Settings > Account details.
claims.fix: The route correctly reaches the enablement page but stops before the subscription and resource-group selections. Keep the path and narrow the note to: 'Entry to the preview subscription-based enablement flow for organisations not using classic Azure Purview data governance pricing. Select an active Azure subscription, then a resource group in that subscription.'

claims.claim: The Defender portal route to app connectors is Settings > Cloud Apps > Connected apps > App Connectors > +Connect an app.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Defender Portal, select Settings. Then choose Cloud Apps. Under Connected apps, select App Connectors. In the App connectors page, select +Connect an app, followed by Dropbox.
claims.fix: The route correctly reaches the connector chooser. Append ' > app' to controls[3].ui.path and replace its note with: 'Choose the app, then complete its connector guide; the Dropbox guide continues through Connect Dropbox and provider authorisation. The general connect-apps page also documents Cloud Apps > Connected apps > Connect an app or Add a new connector.'

claims.claim: The Purview role-group route is Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a member to the role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. The Member parameter specifies who you want to add ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The Pay-as-you-go report is reached through Insider Risk Management > Reports > Pay-as-you-go in the Purview portal.
claims.quote: The following reports are available by navigating to Insider Risk Management > Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal ... Pay-as-you-go: Review pay-as-you-go usage reports

claims.claim: The subscription-based pay-as-you-go enablement page is marked preview.
claims.quote: This featue is in preview.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, custom thresholds; controls table
claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to choose custom trigger thresholds, but the controls table stops at selecting the triggering event.
claims.quote: Choose custom thresholds for trigger indicators on high-volume activity ... controls[1] ends at User performs an exfiltration activity triggering event; no row covers custom thresholds.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Choose custom thresholds for trigger indicators on high-volume activity, such as viewing Power BI reports' and remove 'and adjust thresholds' from the final checklist bullet. This removes the unmatched configuration instructions without adding control rows.
